questions.question: The first sentence of the novel says that a single man with a good fortune "must be in want of" what?
questions.hint: Mrs Bennet has five good reasons to agree with this sentence.
questions.explanation: The sentence is ironic. In the story it is the neighbours, and above all Mrs Bennet, who want a rich single man as a husband for one of their daughters. The man who has just arrived is Mr Bingley.

questions.question: What is the name of Mr Darcy's great estate in Derbyshire?
questions.hint: Elizabeth visits it as a tourist with her aunt and uncle, thinking that the owner is away.
questions.explanation: The housekeeper shows Elizabeth the house and speaks very well of her master. Then Elizabeth meets Darcy himself in the grounds. Longbourn is the Bennets' own home, and Rosings Park belongs to Darcy's aunt, Lady Catherine de Bourgh.

questions.question: Which of the five Bennet sisters runs away with the officer George Wickham?
questions.hint: She is the youngest of the five, and she has followed the regiment to Brighton.
questions.explanation: Lydia is fifteen when the story begins. Her note says they are going to Gretna Green, in Scotland, to marry. In fact the couple hide in London, and it is Mr Darcy who finds them and pays for the marriage.

questions.question: At the first ball, a man will not dance with Elizabeth. He calls her "tolerable", but "not handsome enough to tempt me". Who is he?
questions.hint: Elizabeth hears the remark herself, and it shapes her opinion of him for half the book.
questions.explanation: Darcy says it to his friend Mr Bingley, who wants him to dance. Elizabeth tells the story to her friends as a joke, but she does not forget it. Mr Wickham and Mr Collins have not yet appeared in the story at this point.

questions.question: Which actor played Mr Darcy in the BBC's 1995 television series of Pride and Prejudice?
questions.hint: He played opposite Jennifer Ehle as Elizabeth. One scene, in which his Mr Darcy comes out of a lake in a wet shirt, became famous.
questions.explanation: The six-part series was written by Andrew Davies, and the BBC says that ten million people watched the last episode. Laurence Olivier played Darcy in the 1940 film, and Matthew Macfadyen in the 2005 film with Keira Knightley.

questions.question: Mr Bennet's estate, Longbourn, is entailed: it must pass to a male relative. Who will inherit it when he dies?
questions.hint: He is a distant cousin and a clergyman, and he comes to Longbourn hoping to marry one of the daughters.
questions.explanation: Mr Collins proposes to Elizabeth, who refuses him. A few days later he is engaged to her friend Charlotte Lucas. Because of the entail, he could turn Mrs Bennet and her daughters out of the house as soon as Mr Bennet is dead.

questions.question: In which year was Pride and Prejudice first published?
questions.hint: It came out during the Regency, while Britain was still at war with Napoleon.
questions.explanation: The first edition went on sale in January 1813, in three volumes, for 18 shillings. Austen's name was not on it. The title page said only that it was by the author of Sense and Sensibility, her first published novel, which had come out in 1811.

questions.question: Jane Austen wrote the first version of the novel in 1796 and 1797, when she was about 21. What did she call it then?
questions.hint: The first title names the very thing that misleads Elizabeth about both Darcy and Wickham.
questions.explanation: In November 1797 her father offered "First Impressions" to a London publisher, who said no by return of post. "Elinor and Marianne" is the tempting wrong answer: it was the working title of another early novel, the one that became Sense and Sensibility.

questions.question: Jane Austen died in July 1817, aged 41. In which English city is she buried?
questions.hint: She had moved there about two months before, to be near her doctor. The city is in Hampshire, the county where she was born.
questions.explanation: Austen lies in Winchester Cathedral. Her gravestone says nothing about her books, and a brass plaque was added in 1872 to put that right. Bath and Southampton are cities where she lived before she moved to the village of Chawton in 1809.

questions.question: Austen sold the copyright of Pride and Prejudice to her publisher for one fixed sum. How much was she paid?
questions.hint: It was a single payment, and less than the £150 she had asked for.
questions.explanation: The publisher, Thomas Egerton, kept all the profit, which one scholar puts at about £450 from the first two editions alone. The other sums are real too: a publisher paid £10 for her novel "Susan" in 1803, and Sense and Sensibility earned her £140.
